areas: FETCH and MUTATION checks discard obsolete results without onSuccess
onSuccess runs before synchronous final cache commit
evidence.implication: The observer can confirm callback acceptance and actual committed value after the SWR continuation; a fulfilled fetcher alone is insufficient.

areas: mutate without new data clears FETCH then revalidates
evidence.implication: The existing mutate path remains the fresh-read fallback. Default deduplication alone does not satisfy this optimization.

withArgs merges hook configuration before applying middleware
evidence.implication: Normal middleware receives a real cache. Removing the artificial fetchedAt object as an absent-cache fallback does not change a supported configured path.

findings.resolution: Acceptance requires the matching onSuccess observation, no superseding read, no cache error, and Object.is between the actual cache value and the received value; custom compare is not used as proof.
The separate owner-home subscription retains UNRESOLVED_LIST_SCOPE with a null transport while the selected-workspace subscription remains stable.
LiveChannel.flush selects a currently active subscriber for the key. A departed Board refresh cannot discard a catch-up still required by the persistent Desktop badge.
The acceptance predicate checks required revisions, a copied entry-time baseline, and current cache revisions. A lower committed revision cannot satisfy the obligation through self-comparison.
The continuation requires the same mounted lifetime, visible document, and enabled owner cache. Existing visibility recovery retains its normal catch-up.
The original onSuccess catch records the error only on the matching cache/key/received-value entry and rethrows it. A retained old cache.error is not treated as the current fulfilled read failure.

reviewedInvariants: Sharing is scoped to the exact cache object and key; completed local results are not retained.
An ordinary read must begin after the latest relevant invalidation boundary.
Newer or unversioned pushes during an active read retain their trailing obligation.
Permission errors remain on the existing SWR path without an observer-triggered retry.
Owner/cache retirement prevents adoption and new continuation reads in the departed scope.
Cross-tab adoption retains namespace authorization, previous-cache identity, and revision checks.
Persistent cache hydration, focus freshness, required presence acknowledgement, and revision-before-data contracts are not replaced.

executionEvidence.attribution: Counts are implementer execution results indexed by its source receipt; the independent reviewer did not rerun them.
